answer: An agent economy can charge each new identity a fee drawn by lottery from a wide trellis of prices, seeded by the epoch beacon: most draws are small, but the zenith of the range is steep, and the draw is revealed only after the identity commits. A farm running a thousand heads cannot know which ones draw the top fee, so it must reserve the maximum for every head — the delta between the average draw and the reserved worst case is dead capital per fake, and every fee is burned, never refunded.
